1	\vspace{-6pt}
2	\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
3	\label{sec:discussion}
4	\vspace{-6pt}
5	
6	\paragraph{Limitations.}\looseness=-2
7	Our conclusions rest on $N{=}2$ VLM-to-VLA transitions plus one VLA-to-VLA case, all causal decoders on a single benchmark (LIBERO); flow-matching~\cite{black2024_pi0} and diffusion~\cite{ghosh2024_octo} action heads may behave differently.
8	All findings are correlational ($R^2$ measures decodability, not causal reliance); the $\Delta R^2$--success-rate correlation ($\rho{=}0.583$, $p{=}0.10$; Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_discussion_appendix}) is underpowered ($n{=}9$); each architecture uses a single checkpoint; and the three-tier gradient has $n{=}1$ at Tier~2.
9	All evaluations are open-loop---we probe representational geometry on offline demonstrations without closing the loop through execution---so the link between $\Delta R^2$ and task performance remains indirect.
10	
11	\paragraph{Practical implications and outlook.}\looseness=-2
12	$\Delta R^2 > 0.10$ serves as a lightweight screening signal detectable with linear probes alone, without closed-loop rollouts; a VLA whose exit-layer $R^2$ drops well below its mid-layer peak likely under-utilizes its learned representations.
13	Because action-relevant structure peaks at intermediate layers, downstream modules (reward models, planners) should tap mid-layer features rather than the final hidden state; instruction sensitivity distributed across L1 heads further implies that aggressive early-layer pruning risks degrading instruction following.
14	This cross-architecture decomposition provides a reusable diagnostic framework; extending it to diffusion action heads and closed-loop evaluation are natural next steps.

tool_args.old_string:
When vision-language models are fine-tuned for robotic action prediction, which representational changes are associated with training and which are inherited from the pretrained backbone?
We compare trained and reference checkpoints of three Vision-Language-Action models across four LIBERO task suites via layer-wise probes, attention profiling, and counterfactual perturbations.
We find that VLM-to-VLA fine-tuning is associated with a consistent exit-layer collapse in action-probe decodability ($\Delta R^2 = 0.16$--$0.46$) that is absent in VLA-to-VLA transitions ($\Delta R^2 < 0.10$) and in three NLP instruction-tuning controls ($\Delta R^2 = 0.000$), suggesting this reorganization is specific to action-oriented training rather than a generic fine-tuning artifact.
Complementary analyses reveal that trained VLAs develop substantial sensitivity to instruction content while the dominant attention patterns at early layers largely pre-exist in pretrained backbones.
These findings provide a cross-architecture decomposition of instruction routing in fine-tuned VLAs, disentangling training-associated representational changes from inherited structure.
tool_args.new_string:
When vision-language models (VLMs) are fine-tuned for robotic action prediction, which representational changes are associated with training and which are inherited from the pretrained backbone?
We compare trained and reference checkpoints of three Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models across four LIBERO task suites via layer-wise probes, attention profiling, and counterfactual perturbations.
We find that VLM-to-VLA fine-tuning is associated with a consistent exit-layer collapse in action-probe decodability ($\Delta R^2 = 0.16$--$0.46$) that is absent in VLA-to-VLA transitions ($\Delta R^2 < 0.10$) and in three natural language processing (NLP) instruction-tuning controls ($\Delta R^2 = 0.000$), suggesting this reorganization is specific to action-oriented training rather than a generic fine-tuning artifact.
Complementary analyses reveal that trained VLAs develop substantial sensitivity to instruction content while the dominant attention patterns at early layers largely pre-exist in pretrained backbones.
These findings provide a cross-architecture decomposition of instruction routing in fine-tuned VLAs, disentangling training-associated representational changes from inherited structure.
